note: "Israel was a luxuriant vine, yielding fruit for himself." (Hos 10:1). Replaces the existing broader signifies edge, whose other refs (Ps 80:8, Jer 2:21) state no key.

"the vineyard of the LORD of Hosts is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah are the plant of His delight." (Isa 5:7). The key is stated of the vineyard and the plant; the planted "finest vines" (5:2) take it by context.
"the king of Babylon came to Jerusalem, carried off its king ... so that the kingdom would be brought low" (Ezek 17:12-14). The explanation retells the events; it never says "the vine is".

"I had planted you like a choice vine from the very best seed. How could you turn yourself before Me into a rotten, wild vine?" Ground: planted choice, then turned wild. Addressed to the house of Israel (2:4).
"Glean the remnant of Israel as thoroughly as a vine." Ground: gleaned to the last cluster.
"they will grow grain and blossom like the vine." The tenor is "they" who return, Israel of 14:5; ground: blossoming. Set against Hos 10:1 and left apart.
"He will be like a vine stripped of its unripe grapes, like an olive tree that sheds its blossoms." Ground: the fruit lost before it ripens.
"Your wife will be like a fruitful vine flourishing within your house." Ground: fruitful, within the house.
